questions.q: To use a standard regression model for forecasting, what is the first reframing step?
options: Shuffle the dates so the model cannot memorize order
Turn the series into a table where each row's features come from the past (lags, rolling statistics, calendar fields) and the target is that row's value
Replace the target with the date itself
Remove all seasonality before doing anything else
questions.explain: Supervised forecasting builds one row per time step, with lag and calendar features as inputs and the value to predict as the target.

questions.q: Why does the lesson compute the rolling average as s.shift(1).rolling(7).mean() rather than s.rolling(7).mean()?
options: Shifting makes the rolling average faster to compute
rolling() cannot be applied to a date index
Without the shift, today's own value is included in its own feature, which is leakage
The shift removes the trend from the series
questions.explain: A feature must only use information available before the value being predicted. Shifting by one step keeps today's value out of today's feature.

questions.q: On the lesson's illustrative trending data, gradient boosting on raw sales scored worse than plain linear regression. What is the main reason?
options: Tree-based models cannot extrapolate beyond the range of target values seen in training, so they miss a continuing upward trend
Gradient boosting cannot use lag features
The test set was too large
Linear regression always beats tree models
questions.explain: Trees predict averages of training values, so when the test period exceeds the training range they under-predict. Modeling the change from a rolling average, or detrending, fixes this.

options: Training a different model for each forecast horizon
Forecasting only one step ahead and stopping
Averaging many one-step models trained on shuffled data
Predicting one step ahead, then feeding that prediction back in as a lag feature to predict the next step
questions.explain: Recursive forecasting reuses its own predictions as inputs. Direct forecasting is the alternative, with one model per horizon.

questions.q: Why should cross-validation for forecasting use something like TimeSeriesSplit instead of shuffled K-fold?
options: Shuffled K-fold is slower on time series
TimeSeriesSplit produces larger training sets
Shuffled folds let the model train on the future and test on the past, giving unrealistically good scores
K-fold does not work on numeric targets
questions.explain: Real forecasts only ever use the past to predict the future, so validation must respect that order: training data always precedes test data.
